newsitem.title: UK: Gilts look toppy despite earnings boost - dealers.
newsitem.headline: Gilts look toppy despite earnings boost - dealers.

text.p: 1520 GMT - Gilt futures end higher, but off midsession highs, after a surprise drop in UK earnings and a benign set of U.S. CPI figures. Blip up in PSBR causes no damage. But traders see losses ahead. * September gilt settled 10/32 higher at 114-14
He said the market had been remarkably quiet despite the welter of data thrown at it on Wednesday. The gilt future traded barely more than 60,000 contracts.
Labour market figures, released earlier, showed a 36,500 drop in June unemployment, taking the jobless level to a seven-year low.

But it was a shock fall in May underlying annual average earnings to 4.25 percent from 4.5 that boosted gilts. "The average earnings numbers have increased the chances that the next rise in interest rates will be September rather than August," said Michael Dicks, UK economist at Lehman Brothers.
That more than outweighed an above-forecast public sector debt figure for June.

A PSBR of 4.754 billion stg was reported, some 700 million more than most economists expected. But one-off factors -- an unusually high level of gilt repayments and retiming of VAT receipts -- were quickly siezed upon to explain that away.
"The PSBR was always going to show a large deficit," said Darshini David, UK economist at HSBC Markets.
Minutes from the first meeting of the Bank of England's new monetary policy committee in June, did little for the market. All members voted to raise rates.
Gilts got another small leg-up from a below-forecast 0.1 percent rise in U.S. consumer prices in June. But again, dealers were underwhelmed.
"Even the U.S. trying hard to break through 6.5 percent on the long bond, has not inspired us," one trader said.

He said 10-year gilts, with no supply coming up in the next quarter, were probably well supported, adding that there may be a scramble for the 8.0 percents of 2021 ahead of the Bank of England auction next week.
"They are only selling two billion pounds-worth but I don't buy this argument that the curve will invert substantially."
The gilt/Bund spread sidled in one basis point to 158 on Wednesday but that is against a background of having ballooned out from 133 since early May.
"We've been underperforming Germany for some time," the gilts salesman said. "The gilt market looks cheap internationally but that could be more because the rest of Europe looks expensive."
The September short sterling future settled one basis point higher at 92.84. Traders were comfortable with it pricing in another quarter-point rate rise in the next two months.
